title: When should I ask AI for help?
subtitle: Match the kind of help to the task.
objectives: Choose a task that benefits from ideas.
Recognise when to check an original source.
Identify a decision that belongs to a responsible person.

scenes.title: Let's plan an exhibition!
scenes.narration: Our imaginary science club is planning an exhibition. We need a catchy name, the opening time, and permission to use photos. Should we ask AI for all three in the same way?
scenes.visualAction: Cards for an exhibition name, time and photos appear in sequence.

scenes.title: I need ideas
scenes.narration: For names, we can ask: suggest three short names for an exhibition of simple science experiments. The tool offers possibilities. We choose and improve them. Its suggestion isn't a decision we must follow.
scenes.visualAction: Three imaginary name cards appear, and one is selected.

scenes.title: I need a confirmed detail
scenes.narration: But when does the exhibition open? Check the organiser's announcement or ask the organiser. If an AI answer gives a time, don't rely on that alone. Compare it with the original source.
scenes.visualAction: The proposed time is placed beside the organiser's announcement.

scenes.title: I need permission
scenes.narration: What about sharing visitors' photos? That needs appropriate permission from the people involved and responsible adults. An AI answer cannot grant it. We'll use imaginary illustrations in this activity.
scenes.visualAction: A question mark appears over symbolic photos, with an arrow to a responsible adult.

scenes.title: Choose the right help
scenes.narration: Quick check! A name? Ideas. Opening time? An original source. Sharing people's photos? Human permission. One project, three different kinds of help.
scenes.visualAction: Cards sort into ideas, source and permission.

scenes.title: Your turn
scenes.narration: Imagine a museum trip. Who could help suggest a game for the visit? Where would you check opening hours? Who decides whether you can go? Pause and make your choices.
scenes.visualAction: Museum-trip questions appear with a pause symbol.

scenes.title: You're making the choices
scenes.narration: Get help with ideas, check information, and ask the right people for permission. Before using a real tool, ask a parent about one that's appropriate for your age.
scenes.visualAction: The three key phrases appear with simple motion and a review mark.

reading.title: Ideas: suggest, then choose
reading.text: A tool can suggest names or wording. Compare suggestions with your goal, then choose or improve them yourself.

reading.title: Information: check its source
reading.text: For a real event's opening time, check the organiser's announcement. A time appearing in an AI answer is not enough to confirm it.

reading.title: Permission: ask the right person
reading.text: An AI answer cannot replace someone's permission to use their photo or a parent's permission for an activity. Keep practice examples imaginary.

quiz.question: You need a name for an imaginary exhibition. What could you do?
options: Ask for suggestions and choose a suitable one.
Treat the first suggestion as the only correct name.
Upload a list of every visitor's name.
quiz.explanation: This is an ideas task. The tool suggests; you judge and choose.

quiz.question: An AI answer says the exhibition is on Thursday. How do you check?
options: Repeat the question until the answer sounds reassuring.
Check the organiser's announcement or ask the organiser.
Trust how confident the answer sounds.
quiz.explanation: The organiser is responsible for the schedule. An AI answer alone does not confirm it.

quiz.question: An AI tool suggests sharing your friends' photos. Is that permission?
options: Yes, because the tool suggested it.
Yes, if the photos look good.
No. Permission comes from the people involved and responsible adults.
quiz.explanation: A suggestion cannot give permission on someone else's behalf.

mission.title: Plan an imaginary museum trip
mission.instructions: Write a prompt asking for a museum activity idea. Then name where you would check opening hours and the responsible person you would ask for permission. Use no real personal details.
rubric: I identified an appropriate source for opening hours.
I distinguished a suggestion from permission.

hints.question: What could I ask for?
hints.answer: Names, ideas or wording that you compare and improve yourself.

hints.question: Where do I check the time?
hints.answer: Use the organiser's announcement or an appropriate way of contacting them with a responsible adult.

hints.question: Who can give permission?
hints.answer: The person who owns the decision, or the adult responsible for it. A tool cannot consent for them.

imageBrief.title: Museum trip: choose the right help
imageBrief.composition: A three-way map: a lightbulb for an activity idea, an announcement for visiting hours, and a responsible adult for permission. No exhibition poster or video characters.
imageBrief.altText: Three needs for a museum trip, each linked to a suitable kind of help.
